title: TCP Extensions for Multipath Operation with Multiple Addresses (RFC 8684)
authors: A. Ford; C. Raiciu; M. Handley; O. Bonaventure
architecture: IETF standard for multipath TCP: an MPTCP connection is composed of multiple TCP subflows across different addresses/interfaces.
number_of_paths: One or more subflows per MPTCP connection (standard does not fix a number)
input_parameters: Subflow state (RTT, congestion window, send buffer, available space)
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment (default scheduler specified only loosely)
reordering_handling: Receive-side data-level sequence space with a reassembly buffer and DSS mapping
congestion_control: Coupled congestion control required by the standard (MPTCP semantics)
objective: Provide multipath transport with resource pooling and resilience while remaining fair to single-path TCP
algorithm: Standard specification (not an algorithm paper); default scheduler is a simple policy and is explicitly left replaceable
main_results: N/A - normative specification. Its importance here is that it fixes the interfaces that every later scheduler (including learning-based ones) must work with.
limitations: Normative text: does not prescribe an optimal scheduler, delivery-mode semantics, or reordering policy, which is exactly why the scheduler is a research problem.
research_gap: The RFC exposes a pluggable scheduler point that learning-based and orchestrator-driven schedulers can occupy - but the standard provides no mechanism to signal network-level (orchestrator/slice) objectives into the scheduler.

title: MultiPath TCP: From Theory to Practice
authors: Sébastien Barré; Christoph Paasch; Olivier Bonaventure
architecture: First full MPTCP implementation and experimental evaluation across multiple access networks.
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment
congestion_control: Coupled congestion control (later formalised as LIA)
objective: Demonstrate that MPTCP delivers resource pooling and resilience in practice
algorithm: Default MPTCP scheduler (lowest-RTT-first family) with coupled congestion control
testbed: Real multi-homed testbed with 3G and Wi-Fi interfaces (exact hardware NR in the record retrieved)
main_results: Shows measurable throughput aggregation and improved resilience versus single-path TCP, establishing MPTCP as deployable (exact numbers not verified from the free record).
limitations: Early prototype; the scheduler used is a simple heuristic whose behaviour on very heterogeneous paths later proved problematic (bufferbloat, head-of-line blocking).
research_gap: Motivated the entire subsequent scheduler literature: simple heuristics misbehave on heterogeneous paths, which is the problem DRL schedulers later attack.

title: Design, Implementation and Evaluation of Congestion Control for Multipath TCP
authors: Régel González Usach; Mirja Kühlewind
venue: USENIX Symposium on Networked Systems Design and Implementation (NSDI)
architecture: Design, implementation and experimental evaluation of MPTCP's coupled congestion control.
decision_type: Congestion-window adjustment per subflow (the coupled controller)
objective: Provide resource pooling while remaining fair to competing single-path TCP flows and balancing congestion across paths
algorithm: Coupled congestion control algorithm (LIA-style fluid model with a coupled increase/ decrease rule)
testbed: Real Linux implementation evaluated over emulated and real networks
main_results: Shows that coupling is necessary for fairness and that uncoupled multipath flows starve single-path TCP (exact numbers not verified from the free record).
limitations: Coupling of congestion control does not solve packet scheduling; the interaction between the two remains a source of suboptimality.
research_gap: Establishes that congestion control and scheduling must be co-designed - the insight that motivated later joint DRL schedulers.

title: Experimental evaluation of multipath TCP schedulers
authors: Christoph Paasch; Simone Ferlin; Ozgu Alay; Olivier Bonaventure
venue: Proceedings of the 2014 ACM SIGCOMM workshop on Capacity sharing workshop
architecture: Systematic experimental comparison of MPTCP schedulers over heterogeneous paths.
path_type: Heterogeneous (e.g. Wi-Fi + cellular with different RTT/bandwidth)
input_parameters: Per-subflow RTT, cwnd, send buffer occupancy
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment
reordering_handling: Receive-buffer reassembly with head-of-line blocking measured
objective: Quantify how much the choice of scheduler matters on heterogeneous paths
testbed: Real testbed with emulated asymmetric path characteristics
metrics: Throughput, buffer occupancy at the receiver, reordering
main_results: Demonstrates that the default scheduler can create severe receive-buffer blocking on asymmetric paths, motivating smarter schedulers (exact figures not verified from the free record).
limitations: Small-scale testbed with two paths; no learning-based comparison (2014).
research_gap: Canonical evidence that naive multipath scheduling causes head-of-line blocking - the baseline any new scheduler must beat.

title: Low-Latency Scheduling in MPTCP
authors: Per Hurtig; Karl-Johan Grinnemo; Anna Brunstrom; Simone Ferlin; Ozgu Alay; Nicolas Kuhn
architecture: Design and evaluation of low-latency MPTCP schedulers targeting latency-sensitive traffic.
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment optimising for low delay (a blocking-estimation/earliest-delivery style rule)
reordering_handling: Explicitly considered: the scheduler is designed to reduce reordering-induced latency
objective: Minimise end-to-end latency (rather than maximise throughput) for latency-sensitive applications
algorithm: Latency-optimised scheduling rules derived from an analysis of the delay components of MPTCP
testbed: Linux MPTCP implementation evaluated in emulated and real networks
main_results: Shows that latency-optimised scheduling reduces completion time for short flows versus the default scheduler (exact figures not verified from the free record).
limitations: Rule-based; assumes reasonably accurate RTT estimation; does not learn from network state or coordinate with an orchestrator.
research_gap: A strong classical latency-oriented baseline that learning-based schedulers must outperform - and a natural candidate for the 'scheduler' slot in a hybrid LLM/DRL controller.

title: Multipath QUIC
authors: Quentin De Coninck; Olivier Bonaventure
venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on emerging Networking EXperiments and Technologies (ACM CoNEXT)
architecture: Extension of QUIC to multipath operation: a single QUIC connection spanning multiple paths, with a pluggable scheduler.
decision_type: Packet-to-path assignment (scheduling) plus path management
reordering_handling: Connection-level packet-number space allows the receiver to reassemble; the paper studies the effect of scheduling on reordering
congestion_control: Coupled congestion control inherited from MPTCP concepts
objective: Demonstrate that multipath can be added to QUIC and evaluate the resulting performance
algorithm: Multipath QUIC design with a lowest-RTT style scheduler; the paper's contribution is the protocol extension and its evaluation
testbed: Real implementation (userspace QUIC) evaluated over emulated networks
main_results: Shows that multipath QUIC aggregates bandwidth and survives path failure, and identifies scheduling/reordering as the key implementation challenge (exact figures not verified from the free record).
limitations: Early design; scheduler is a simple heuristic and the interaction with QUIC's loss recovery is delicately handled.
research_gap: Opens the MPQUIC scheduler design space that later learning-based MPQUIC schedulers (e.g. multi-agent RL and PPO-based approaches) occupy.

title: The QUIC Transport Protocol: Design and Internet-Scale Deployment
authors: Adam Langley; Alistair Riddoch; Alyssa Wilk; Antonio Vicente; Charles Krasic; Dan Zhang; Fan Yang; Fedor Kouranov; Ian Swett; Janardhan Iyengar; Jeff Bailey; Jeremy Dorfman
venue: Proceedings of the Conference of the ACM Special Interest Group on Data Communication (ACM SIGCOMM)
architecture: Design and Internet-scale deployment measurement of QUIC.
number_of_paths: One (single path); included because MPQUIC scheduling depends on QUIC's connection-level packet numbering
decision_type: N/A (single path)
reordering_handling: Connection-level packet numbers make reordering observable and avoid TCP's ambiguity
congestion_control: Cubic and BBR support in QUIC
objective: Report the design and the measured deployment of QUIC at Google scale
metrics: Handshake latency, search latency, rebuffer rate, throughput
main_results: Reports measurable latency and rebuffering improvements over TCP+TLS at Internet scale (exact figures in the paper; not re-verified here).
limitations: Not a multipath paper; its relevance is architectural.
research_gap: QUIC's connection-level packet number space is the enabler for MPQUIC schedulers that must reason about reordering - context for any AI scheduler targeting MPQUIC.

title: ReLeS: A Neural Adaptive Multipath Scheduler based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Han Zhang; Wenzhong Li; Shaohua Gao; Xiaoliang Wang; Baoliu Ye
venue: IEEE INFOCOM 2019 - IEEE Conference on Computer Communications
architecture: ReLeS: a DRL-based MPTCP packet scheduler implemented in the Linux kernel with an asynchronous training pipeline.
path_type: Heterogeneous (per abstract's framing of 'diverse QoS characteristics')
scheduler_location: Linux kernel (implementation stated in the abstract); a separate training process runs asynchronously
decision_type: Packet scheduling policy generated by a learned neural network
packet_or_flow: Packet-level (implied by the abstract's framing of multipath packet scheduling)
objective: A 'comprehensive reward function that takes diverse QoS characteristics into consideration' (individual terms not stated in the abstract)
algorithm: Deep reinforcement learning producing the scheduling policy, plus an asynchronous training algorithm that decouples packet scheduling, data collection and neural-network training so scheduling can run in real time
testbed: Evaluated 'over both emulated and real network conditions' (Linux kernel implementation)
baselines: Not named in the abstract; the full text is closed access (Unpaywall: closed with zero OA locations; no arXiv version; no author PDF)
main_results: Qualitative only: 'ReLeS significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art schedulers.' No numbers are stated in the abstract, and no open-access full text was located (Unpaywall: closed; no arXiv version).
limitations: The abstract exposes no state space, action space, reward terms, baselines or hyperparameters, and the full text is paywalled - so the paper cannot be quantitatively compared or reproduced from open sources. That is itself a reproducibility finding.
research_gap: ReLeS is the canonical 'DRL scheduler for MPTCP' citation, yet its design is not openly reproducible. A PhD contribution could be a fully open, reproducible DRL/LLM scheduler with published state/action/reward and code.

title: DeepCC: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Congestion Control for Multi-Path TCP Based on Self-Attention
authors: Bo He; Jingyu Wang; Qi Qi; Haifeng Sun; Jianxin Liao; Chunning Du; Xiang Yang; Zhu Han
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
architecture: DeepCC: multi-agent DRL congestion control and split-ratio control for MPTCP. Agents run in Linux userspace as daemons and write kernel sysctl parameters; kernel exposes cwnd, RTT, loss and split ratios.
number_of_paths: Four MPTCP subflows running simultaneously in the evaluation
path_type: Heterogeneous, emulated with Linux tc/ethtool (delay, bandwidth, random loss per subflow)
scheduler_location: Sender side, split kernel (data path, sysctl state) / userspace (DRL agents)
input_parameters: Per-subflow self state (goodput x, cwnd c, RTT k, jitter v, w, loss l) plus a self-attention-weighted embedding of the other subflows' states - a 12-dimensional state vector per agent i at epoch t
path_metrics: Average goodput, congestion window, RTT, jitter, loss, split ratio
decision_type: Continuous control of two quantities per subflow: the change to the traffic split ratio and the multiplicative coefficient for the congestion window
packet_or_flow: Packet-level (split ratio determines per-packet subflow assignment; cwnd controls sending rate)
reordering_handling: Goodput is defined as bytes received correctly and sequentially, so reordering is penalised through the reward rather than handled by a dedicated mechanism
congestion_control: The DRL agents themselves replace/control congestion control (cwnd is set by the action); compared against LIA, OLIA, BALIA, wVegas and DRL baselines DRL-CC and SmartCC
objective: Increase total goodput (bytes received correctly and sequentially per unit time) and reduce congestion; multi-agent general-sum game solved toward Nash equilibrium
algorithm: MAPOKTR - Multi-Agent Policy Optimization using Kronecker-Factored Trust Region (ACKTR-derived with K-FAC natural gradient, PPO-style clipped ratio and a point-probability-distance penalty); one agent per subflow; BiLSTM (size 32) encoder over other subflows' states with self-attention
simulator: No simulator - real Linux testbed: sender Dell i7-8700, 32 GB RAM, Ubuntu 16.04, MPTCP v0.93 on Linux 4.9.x; path characteristics limited with tc and ethtool; receiver on a separate desktop via a Gigabit switch; packets captured with tcpdump and analysed with scapy; iPerf3 for load and TRex replaying real traces for background traffic
testbed: Single-sender emulated heterogeneous testbed (not real radio)
traffic_model: Bulk FTP file transfers of 2 MB and 4 MB, plus iPerf3 and TRex background traffic
baselines: DRL-CC, SmartCC, LIA, OLIA, BALIA, wVegas; algorithm comparison against MAACKTR and MADDPG; architecture ablations (FC, FC+PSA, SSA without PSA); reward ablations (fair, efficient, fair-efficient)
metrics: Total goodput, average jitter (difference of consecutive RTTs), per-path goodput ratio, CPU and memory usage, convergence time, robustness in unseen environments
main_results: Self-attention reduces convergence time by about 50% and increases goodput by about 80% compared with common neural-network structures; the fair-efficient reward outperforms single-objective rewards.
limitations: All paths are emulated on one host with tc/ethtool rather than real Wi-Fi/LTE radio; bulk FTP traffic only (no video/web); the scheduler is evaluated per-connection rather than in a sliced/core-network setting; no orchestrator or slice objective is involved.
research_gap: DeepCC shows that learning can jointly control congestion control and split ratio, but it is invisible to the network: no slice/SLA objective, no orchestrator interface, no ATSSS/UPF integration. Connecting such a scheduler to an orchestrator that supplies objectives is an open problem.

title: Leveraging Coupled BBR and Adaptive Packet Scheduling to Boost MPTCP
authors: Jiangping Han; Kaiping Xue; Yitao Xing; Jian Li; Wenjia Wei; David S. L. Wei; Guoliang Xue
architecture: Coupling BBR congestion control with adaptive packet scheduling for MPTCP.
input_parameters: Per-subflow delivery rate and RTT estimates from BBR, plus scheduler state
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment coordinated with BBR's rate estimate
reordering_handling: Scheduling is adapted to reduce reordering under BBR
objective: Boost MPTCP throughput by adapting the scheduler to BBR's delivery-rate estimates
algorithm: Adaptive packet scheduling coupled to BBR
ml_method: No - BBR-derived analytical congestion control plus adaptive scheduling heuristics
testbed: Linux MPTCP testbed with emulated heterogeneous paths
baselines: Default MPTCP scheduler, other BBR-based MPTCP variants
main_results: Reports throughput gains over baseline MPTCP scheduling when BBR is used (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Contains no machine learning; the authors argue against RL on CPU-cost and generalisation grounds. Do not describe this paper as AI-native or learning-based.
research_gap: Demonstrates CC-scheduler coupling - evidence that schedulers cannot be designed in isolation from the controller, which strengthens the case for joint learning-based control.

title: BBR-Based Congestion Control and Packet Scheduling for Bottleneck Fairness Considered Multipath TCP in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
authors: Wenjia Wei; Kaiping Xue; Jiangping Han; Yitao Xing; David S. L. Wei; Peilin Hong
architecture: BBR-based congestion control with packet scheduling designed for bottleneck fairness in heterogeneous MPTCP.
path_metrics: Delivery rate, RTT, loss, bottleneck share
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment plus rate control
objective: Maintain bottleneck fairness between MPTCP subflows and competing flows while improving throughput
algorithm: BBR-based coupled control with a fairness-aware scheduler
ml_method: No - BBR-based congestion control with fairness-aware scheduling heuristics
testbed: Linux testbed with emulated heterogeneous paths
main_results: Reports improved fairness at the shared bottleneck relative to loss-based MPTCP (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Contains no machine learning; like Coupled BBR it argues against RL on complexity and generalisation grounds.
research_gap: Fairness across multipath subflows is treated as a transport-level concern; network-level fairness (across slices/tenants) is not considered - a gap for orchestrator-integrated multipath.

title: BLEST: Blocking estimation-based MPTCP scheduler for heterogeneous networks
authors: Simone Ferlin; Ozgu Alay; Olivier Mehani; Roksana Boreli
venue: 2016 IFIP Networking Conference (IFIP Networking) and Workshops
architecture: BLEST: blocking-estimation-based MPTCP scheduler for heterogeneous networks.
input_parameters: Estimated head-of-line blocking delay per subflow, derived from RTT and send-rate estimates
path_metrics: Estimated blocking delay, RTT, congestion window
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment that avoids subflows predicted to cause head-of-line blocking
reordering_handling: Core of the design: estimates whether sending on a slow subflow would block in-order delivery and avoids it
objective: Minimise head-of-line blocking / improve goodput on heterogeneous paths
algorithm: Blocking-estimation heuristic (compute, for each subflow, the delay it would impose on the next in-order segment; penalise accordingly)
testbed: Linux MPTCP implementation evaluated in emulated and real heterogeneous networks
baselines: minRTT (default), DAPS, OTIAS, single-path TCP - NOTE: Round-Robin is NOT a baseline in BLEST
metrics: Goodput, head-of-line blocking delay, completion time
main_results: Substantially reduces head-of-line blocking and improves goodput relative to the default scheduler on asymmetric paths (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Heuristic with no learning; relies on accurate send-rate estimation; does not consider application or network-level objectives.
research_gap: BLEST is the classical reordering-aware baseline that any learning-based scheduler must beat - and the natural comparison point for a DRL/LLM scheduler that must also respect network-level objectives.

title: ECF: An MPTCP Path Scheduler to Manage Heterogeneous Paths
authors: Reza Poorzare; Oliver P. Waldhorst
venue: Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on emerging Networking EXperiments and Technologies (ACM CoNEXT)
architecture: ECF: an MPTCP path scheduler that manages heterogeneous paths by explicitly considering the receive buffer and the in-flight window.
input_parameters: Per-subflow RTT, cwnd, slow-start state, receive-buffer size, in-flight bytes
path_metrics: RTT, cwnd, in-flight bytes, receive buffer occupancy
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment with an explicit penalty term for the fastest path (to avoid overloading it)
reordering_handling: Accounts for receive-buffer blocking by limiting in-flight data on slower paths
objective: Improve goodput on heterogeneous paths by balancing the receive buffer across subflows
algorithm: ECF heuristic (penalise the best path by the RTT difference and track per-path in-flight/receive-buffer state)
testbed: Linux MPTCP implementation evaluated in emulated heterogeneous networks
baselines: Default (minRTT), DAPS, BLEST - NOTE: Round-Robin is NOT a baseline in ECF
main_results: Reports higher goodput than the default and competing schedulers on heterogeneous paths (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Rule-based and tuned to the receive-buffer regime; no learning; no network-level objective.
research_gap: Along with BLEST, ECF defines the classical state of the art that learning-based schedulers are benchmarked against - useful as a baseline in a PhD evaluation.

title: Peekaboo: Learning-Based Multipath Scheduling for Dynamic Heterogeneous Environments
authors: Hongjia Wu; Ozgu Alay; Anna Brunstrom; Simone Ferlin; Giuseppe Caso
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
architecture: Peekaboo: a learning-based multipath scheduler for dynamic heterogeneous environments.
scheduler_location: Sender-side MPTCP scheduler (kernel implementation with a learning component)
input_parameters: Per-path state including RTT, delivery rate, congestion window and buffer estimates
path_metrics: RTT, delivery rate, cwnd, path availability
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment learned from observed path behaviour
reordering_handling: Scheduler learns to account for reordering and blocking
objective: Maximise goodput/latency performance in dynamic heterogeneous environments where path characteristics change
algorithm: LinUCB contextual bandit selecting the scheduling action from observed path context
ml_method: Contextual bandit (LinUCB, d=6) - NOT deep RL
testbed: Linux MPTCP testbed with emulated dynamic heterogeneous paths
baselines: Default MPTCP scheduler; BLEST; ECF; DAPS (Round-Robin appears as a baseline only in this paper, not in BLEST/ECF)
main_results: Reports improved performance over heuristic schedulers when path characteristics change over time (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Contextual bandit with a linear model over a 6-dimensional context - a deliberately lightweight learner, not deep RL; no interface to network-level objectives; evaluation remains transport-level.
research_gap: Peekaboo is the closest classical work to 'learning scheduler', yet it never receives an objective from the network. Supplying objectives from an orchestrator (and proving SLA benefit) is the open step.

title: CMT-QA: Quality-Aware Adaptive Concurrent Multipath Data Transfer in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
authors: Changqiao Xu; Tianjiao Liu; Jianfeng Guan; Hongke Zhang; Gabriel-Miro Muntean
architecture: CMT-QA: quality-aware adaptive concurrent multipath data transfer in heterogeneous wireless networks.
input_parameters: Path quality measurements (bandwidth, delay, loss) and receive-buffer state
decision_type: Data-chunk-to-path assignment and rate adaptation based on measured path quality
reordering_handling: Explicitly addresses reordering induced by path diversity
objective: Improve goodput and QoS while limiting reordering damage
testbed: Simulation and/or emulation of heterogeneous wireless paths
main_results: Reports improved throughput and reduced reordering relative to baseline CMT (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Pre-5G transport (SCTP/CMT) that is not deployed in 5G cores; heuristic rather than learned.
research_gap: Historical baseline for quality-aware multipath scheduling; its objective set (goodput vs reordering) is the same trade-off that modern AI schedulers must handle.

title: Bandwidth-Efficient Multipath Transport Protocol for Quality-Guaranteed Real-Time Video Over Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
authors: Jiyan Wu; Chau Yuen; Bo Cheng; Yuan Yang; Ming Wang; Junliang Chen
architecture: Bandwidth-efficient multipath transport protocol providing quality guarantees for real-time video over heterogeneous wireless networks.
input_parameters: Path bandwidth/delay estimates and video frame deadlines/importance
decision_type: Frame/packet-to-path assignment with quality guarantees
reordering_handling: Deadline-aware reordering handling for video frames
objective: Maximise delivered video quality subject to bandwidth efficiency and deadline constraints
baselines: Baseline multipath transport without quality guarantees
metrics: Video quality (PSNR/quality level), bandwidth efficiency, deadline miss rate
main_results: Reports quality guarantees at reduced bandwidth cost versus baseline multipath transport (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Application-specific (video); heuristic; no learning and no network-level control interface.
research_gap: Shows that multipath scheduling can carry application-level objectives; extending that to network-level (slice/SLA) objectives via an orchestrator is unexplored here.

title: Tokens, Not Packets: Rethinking the Multipath QUIC Scheduling Interface
authors: Hendrik Cech; Patrick Bokelmann; Nitinder Mohan
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Applied Networking Research Workshop
architecture: Position/measurement work arguing that the MPQUIC scheduling interface should operate on tokens rather than packets.
input_parameters: Scheduling interface state (the paper's argument is that the current packet-oriented interface is the wrong abstraction)
decision_type: Redesign of the scheduling interface (token-based rather than packet-based)
packet_or_flow: Both (the paper argues the interface must expose flow-level information)
objective: Expose a scheduling interface that lets schedulers make better decisions by decoupling flow-level policy from packet-level mechanics
algorithm: Interface redesign with measurement of existing schedulers
testbed: Measurement study on real MPQUIC implementations
main_results: Shows that the packet-based scheduling interface constrains what schedulers can express (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Interface/measurement contribution rather than a new scheduler; very recent (2026).
research_gap: Directly relevant: a token/flow-level interface is precisely what an orchestrator or LLM agent would need in order to express network-level objectives to a multipath scheduler.

title: A Stream-Aware Multipath QUIC Scheduler for Heterogeneous Paths
authors: Alexander Rabitsch; Per Hurtig; Anna Brunstrom
venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on the Evolution, Performance, and Interoperability of QUIC
architecture: Stream-aware MPQUIC scheduler for heterogeneous paths.
input_parameters: Per-path state plus per-stream information (stream priorities/requirements)
decision_type: Stream-and-packet-to-path assignment
reordering_handling: Stream-level reassembly limits cross-stream head-of-line blocking
objective: Improve performance for multi-stream applications over heterogeneous paths
main_results: Reports improved multi-stream performance versus the default scheduler (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Heuristic and stream-oriented; no learning, no network-level objective.
research_gap: Supports the argument that schedulers need richer (flow/stream) context - the same context an LLM agent could reason about.

title: Multipath QUIC for Access Traffic Steering Switching and Splitting in 5G Advanced
authors: Apostolis K. Salkintzis; Mirja Kühlewind; Stefan Rommer; Rainer Liebhart
architecture: Multipath QUIC applied to 5G ATSSS: using MPQUIC as the multipath transport for access traffic steering, switching and splitting in the 5G core.
scheduler_location: UE and UPF sides of the ATSSS architecture (MPQUIC endpoints)
input_parameters: Per-access path state; ATSSS policy from the network
decision_type: Steering/switching/splitting of traffic across 3GPP and non-3GPP access
reordering_handling: MPQUIC reordering handling at the receiver
objective: Realise ATSSS with a standards-compatible multipath transport and evaluate its performance
main_results: Demonstrates MPQUIC as a viable ATSSS transport with performance benefits over single-access operation (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Standards/prototype orientation; the steering policy itself is not learned and does not optimise network-level objectives.
research_gap: Directly relevant: ATSSS is the 5G-core hook where a multipath scheduler meets network policy. The policy engine that would drive it with AI/LLM objectives is absent.

title: Cost optimized multipath scheduling in 5G for Video-on-Demand traffic
authors: Markus Amend; Veselin Rakocevic; Joachim Habermann
venue: 2021 IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference (WCNC)
architecture: Cost-optimised multipath scheduling for 5G multi-connectivity carrying video-on-demand traffic.
input_parameters: Per-leg cost and performance; video segment requirements
decision_type: Traffic split per leg
objective: Minimise delivery cost while satisfying video-on-demand quality
main_results: Reports cost reductions for VoD delivery under multipath (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Cost-oriented and application-specific; no learning and no orchestrator integration.
research_gap: Cost/SLA trade-offs in multipath are exactly what an orchestrator would optimise; the coupling of multipath decisions to orchestration objectives is not addressed.

title: GCLR: GNN-Based Cross Layer Optimization for Multipath TCP by Routing
authors: Ting Zhu; Xiaohui Chen; Li Chen; Weidong Wang; Guo Wei
architecture: GCLR: GNN-based cross-layer optimisation for MPTCP by routing, i.e. choosing routes for subflows to improve MPTCP performance.
scheduler_location: Cross-layer: routing decision coupled to the MPTCP scheduler
input_parameters: Network topology and link state, path performance history
decision_type: Route selection for subflows (path-level), affecting scheduling
packet_or_flow: Flow/path-level routing with packet-level scheduling beneath
reordering_handling: Routing choices are used to reduce path asymmetry
objective: Improve MPTCP goodput by routing subflows over better path combinations
algorithm: Graph neural network predicting path performance + routing optimisation
main_results: Reports improved MPTCP performance from GNN-guided routing (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Optimises routing, not the scheduler itself; no network-level objective; GNN retraining requirements.
research_gap: Shows learning can inform the path layer of multipath transport; combining that with a learned scheduler under orchestrator objectives is still open.

title: Multipath TCP Meets Reinforcement Learning: A Novel Energy-Efficient Scheduling Approach in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
authors: Pingping Dong; Rongcheng Shen; Qian Wang; Yuning Zuo; Yajing Li; Dian Zhang; Lianming Zhang; Wenjun Yang
architecture: Energy-efficient MPTCP scheduling using reinforcement learning in heterogeneous wireless networks.
scheduler_location: Sender-side MPTCP scheduler with an RL agent
input_parameters: Per-path state plus energy/consumption model of the interfaces
path_metrics: RTT, throughput, loss, energy per bit
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment minimising energy
objective: Minimise energy consumption while maintaining acceptable performance
algorithm: Reinforcement learning (exact variant per the paper)
main_results: Reports energy savings relative to the default scheduler (exact figures not re-verified here).
limitations: Energy-only objective at the transport layer; no network-level objective and no orchestrator interface.
research_gap: Energy is a first-class objective for 6G; an orchestrator-level energy objective driving multipath selection is not addressed in this line of work.

title: DAPS: Intelligent delay-aware packet scheduling for multipath transport
authors: Nicolas Kuhn; Emmanuel Lochin; Ahlem Mifdaoui; Golam Sarwar; Olivier Mehani; Roksana Boreli
architecture: DAPS: delay-aware packet scheduling for multipath transport
input_parameters: Per-path delay estimates and delivery-rate estimates
decision_type: Packet-to-subflow assignment minimising expected delivery delay
objective: Minimise delivery delay across paths
algorithm: DAPS heuristic (compare estimated delivery times across subflows)
main_results: NA
limitations: Heuristic; no learning; transport-level objective only.
research_gap: One of the earliest delay-aware MPTCP schedulers and a standard baseline for latency-oriented multipath work.

title: An Improved MPQUIC Scheduler Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: NA
venue: IEICE Transactions on Information and Systems
architecture: Improved MPQUIC scheduler based on multi-agent reinforcement learning
decision_type: Packet-to-path assignment learned by multiple agents
objective: Improve MPQUIC performance on heterogeneous paths
main_results: NA
limitations: Retrieved at metadata level (IEICE Transactions on Information and Systems).
research_gap: One of the few multi-agent RL MPQUIC schedulers; no network-level (orchestrator/slice) objective.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Access Traffic Splitting in 5G Core System
authors: NA
architecture: Deep reinforcement learning for access traffic splitting decision-making in the 5G core
decision_type: Access traffic split ratio per flow
objective: NA
